page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 8 physical cores and 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 200 GB SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core scoring 3671.98 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 38.12 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs in the top tier at 17.51 GB/sec. Multi-core and memory performance generally fall into the average tier, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 10089.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 17608.73. However, memory bandwidth is weaker under certain workloads, with the Passmark memory score falling into the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with medium 7B model text generation scoring in the bottom 10% at 5.45 tokens/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server represents a compute-oriented resource density suited for workloads that require strong single-threaded performance but can tolerate shared CPU resources. It is well-suited for tasks such as static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference due to its lower memory-to-core ratio and weaker memory benchmark scores.
